steps.tx: **Arginine vasopressin deficiency**, also called central diabetes insipidus, and **arginine vasopressin resistance**, also called nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, both produce large volumes of dilute urine. **Primary polydipsia** produces dilute urine too, but the plasma is driven down by drinking. The plasma sodium is often normal in diabetes insipidus if the person can drink freely.

vis.caption: Posterior pituitary and a collecting-duct cell with a vasopressin receptor and aquaporin channels. The drawing shows the pathway. It does not separate deficiency from resistance. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: In the **water deprivation test**, diabetes insipidus fails to concentrate the urine above about 300 mOsm/kg while plasma osmolality rises above 295 mOsm/kg. **Desmopressin** then raises urine osmolality by more than 50 percent in arginine vasopressin deficiency, and it does little when the kidney is resistant. Primary polydipsia concentrates the urine during deprivation.

vis.alt: Water deprivation graph: primary polydipsia concentrates, central diabetes insipidus rises after desmopressin, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus does not.
vis.caption: The graph uses the older names. Primary polydipsia concentrates during deprivation. Central diabetes insipidus rises by more than 50 percent after desmopressin. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus stays flat. The footnote lists thiazides and amiloride for lithium. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: After hypertonic saline, a **copeptin** at or below 4 point 9 pmol/L indicates arginine vasopressin deficiency. A baseline copeptin at or above 21 point 4 pmol/L indicates arginine vasopressin resistance and can spare the patient a deprivation test. Copeptin is the stable C-terminal piece of the vasopressin precursor. A value between those cutoffs still needs the clinical context.

rows: 4.9 pmol/L or lower after hypertonic saline

steps.tx: **Desmopressin** is the treatment for arginine vasopressin deficiency. Too much desmopressin causes **hyponatremia**. **Adipsic diabetes insipidus**, usually after hypothalamic injury, is dangerous because thirst does not protect the sodium, so fluid intake is prescribed rather than left to thirst. A high sodium means access to water is impaired or thirst is broken.

left.title: Deficiency with intact thirst
points: Desmopressin replaces the missing hormone
Too much desmopressin causes hyponatremia
Free access to water often keeps sodium normal
Teach the patient to hold a dose if they do not drink

right.title: Adipsic diabetes insipidus
points: Thirst is broken after hypothalamic injury
Sodium is not protected by drinking
Fluid intake has to be prescribed
Desmopressin alone is not a safe plan

steps.tx: **Lithium** is the classic cause of arginine vasopressin resistance. **Amiloride** is the preferred diuretic because it blocks lithium entry through the epithelial sodium channel. A **thiazide** and a low-solute diet reduce urine volume when resistance is fixed and desmopressin will not work. Stopping lithium is the best reversal when the psychiatric plan allows it.

rows: Lowers urine volume when resistance persists

steps.tx: After pituitary surgery the water balance can be **triphasic**: early diabetes insipidus, then a syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis as stored vasopressin leaks, then permanent diabetes insipidus if the neurons were destroyed. A sodium that falls in the middle phase is not a reason to increase **desmopressin**. Hold the drug and restrict water until the leak passes.

steps.tx: **Pregnancy** can unmask arginine vasopressin deficiency because placental **vasopressinase** breaks down vasopressin. **Desmopressin** is resistant to that enzyme and is the drug used in pregnancy. The mother may first present with polyuria in the second half of pregnancy. After delivery the enzyme falls and the dose often can be reduced.

left.title: Native vasopressin in pregnancy
points: Placental vasopressinase breaks it down
A mild deficiency can be unmasked
Polyuria may start in later pregnancy
It is a poor replacement in this setting

right.title: Desmopressin
points: Resists vasopressinase
Drug used for deficiency in pregnancy
Dose is reviewed after delivery
Hyponatremia is still the overdose risk

steps.tx: The **plasma sodium** is often normal in diabetes insipidus if the person can drink freely. A high sodium means access to water is impaired or thirst is broken. **Polyuria** with a low-normal sodium suggests **primary polydipsia** until the deprivation test or copeptin says otherwise. Do not start desmopressin on a low sodium.

left.title: High sodium with polyuria
points: Access to water is poor or thirst is broken
Diabetes insipidus is likely
Adipsic disease is the dangerous form
Replace water before you chase a rare cause

right.title: Low-normal sodium with polyuria
points: Primary polydipsia is the first thought
The plasma is diluted by drinking
Desmopressin can cause severe hyponatremia
Prove the diagnosis before you treat
